senses.definition: Every one of two or more things or people, thought of separately.
senses.example: Put one seed in each cup.

senses.definition: Every one in a group, taken one at a time.
senses.example: Each of the two dogs got a bowl of water.

senses.definition: Very ready or excited to do something.
senses.example: We were eager to open the time capsule.

senses.definition: The part of your body you use to hear, including the part you can see on the side of your head.
senses.example: I held the shell next to my ear.

senses.definition: The part of a corn plant that holds the kernels, or a similar part of a grain plant.
senses.example: We pulled the leaves off an ear of corn.

senses.definition: A thin layer of tissue in the ear that moves when sound reaches it.
senses.example: Air vibrations make the eardrum move slightly back and forth.

senses.definition: Near the beginning of a time or before the expected time.
senses.example: We took an early bus to school.

senses.definition: Before the expected or usual time.
senses.example: The rain started early today.

senses.definition: To get something because of work, effort, or how you act.
senses.example: We can earn a spot in the tournament by winning two games.

senses.definition: The planet where people, and all other life known so far, live. The name of our planet is written Earth.
senses.example: Pictures from space show white clouds above Earth.

senses.definition: The soil or ground beneath your feet.
senses.example: The earth crumbled when I tried to pick up a handful.

senses.definition: A shaking of the ground that usually happens when rocks suddenly slip past one another deep below the surface.
senses.example: The earthquake made the windows rattle.

senses.definition: One of the four main directions, opposite west.
senses.example: We used a compass to find east.

senses.definition: Toward the direction opposite west.
senses.example: We walked east from the bridge.

senses.definition: Not hard to do, understand, or handle.
senses.example: The first question was easy to answer.

senses.definition: To take food into your mouth and swallow it, usually after chewing.
senses.example: I will eat the peach when I get home.

senses.definition: A sound that returns after bouncing off a surface.
senses.example: I heard an echo when I called across the valley.

senses.definition: Finding where things are by making sounds and listening for the echoes that bounce back.
senses.example: Some bats use echolocation to find insects in the dark.

senses.definition: An event in space when one object blocks another from view or moves into its shadow.
senses.example: During a lunar eclipse, Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon.

senses.definition: To block something from view or make it seem less noticeable by comparison.
senses.example: The Moon can briefly eclipse the Sun.

senses.definition: A change over time in the kinds of living things in a place.
senses.example: Grasses grew first and young trees grew later during ecological succession in the old field.

senses.definition: The living things in a place, the nonliving things around them, and the ways they affect one another.
senses.example: In a pond ecosystem, light, water, plants, frogs, and insects all connect.

senses.definition: A living thing that changes the shape or physical conditions of a place used by other living things.
senses.example: A beaver is an ecosystem engineer when its dam creates a pond.

senses.definition: A line where two faces of a solid shape meet, or the outside of a flat shape.
senses.example: I ran my finger along one edge of the cube.

senses.definition: Learning and teaching that help people gain knowledge and skills, often at school.
senses.example: The library gave my grandfather a place to keep learning after his school education ended.

senses.definition: A result or change caused by something else.
senses.example: Adding more water had one clear effect: the paint became thinner.

senses.definition: Work or energy you use to try to do something.
senses.example: It took a lot of effort to push the cart uphill.

senses.definition: A rounded thing laid by many kinds of animals that can hold the food and space a young animal needs to start growing. People eat eggs from some birds, such as chickens.
senses.example: A baby bird hatched from an egg in the nest.

senses.definition: Coming next after seventh in an order.
senses.example: The eighth runner wore a bright blue shirt.

senses.definition: One of eight equal parts.
senses.example: I ate one eighth of the pie.

senses.definition: One or the other of two choices.
senses.example: You may sit on either bench.

senses.definition: One of two things, without saying which.
senses.example: Both pencils are sharp, so either will work.

senses.definition: Also, used after saying that something is not true.
senses.example: I don’t like onions, and my brother doesn’t either.

senses.definition: Made or planned with many parts and details.
senses.example: She built an elaborate castle from cardboard.

senses.definition: To give more information about an idea or what you said.
senses.example: Could you elaborate on your plan for the new garden?

senses.definition: How much time goes by between the start and end of an activity or event.
senses.example: The elapsed time between our two stops was forty minutes.

senses.definition: The joint that lets the arm bend between the upper arm and the forearm.
senses.example: I rested my elbow on the desk.

senses.definition: To push or touch someone with the hard part of your bent arm.
senses.example: My friend elbowed me gently to get my attention.

senses.definition: To choose someone for a position by voting.
senses.example: The students will elect a class leader on Friday.

senses.definition: Using, producing, or related to electricity.
senses.example: The electric lights came on when we opened the door.

senses.definition: Full of strong excitement.
senses.example: The crowd created an electric feeling before the final song.

senses.definition: A substance that lets charged particles move through it, such as the substance between the ends of a battery.
senses.example: Moving particles inside the electrolyte help the battery work.

senses.definition: A magnet that gets its magnetic field from flowing electricity.
senses.example: The crane’s electromagnet could let go of metal when its power was switched off.

senses.definition: A tiny part of matter with a negative electric charge. Electrons are found around the centers of atoms.
senses.example: Electrons can move through the copper wire in a circuit.

senses.definition: A basic chemical substance made of just one kind of atom, such as gold or oxygen.
senses.example: Iron is an element used to make steel.

senses.definition: One part or feature of something that has several parts.
senses.example: A surprise ending is one element of this story.

senses.definition: Basic or suitable for someone beginning to learn a subject.
senses.example: The book introduces elementary drawing techniques.

senses.definition: Related to the first years of school.
senses.example: I joined the chess club in elementary school.

senses.definition: A very large land mammal with thick legs, big ears, and a long trunk.
senses.example: The elephant used its trunk to pick up leaves.

senses.definition: A moving platform or room that carries people or things up and down inside a building.
senses.example: Take the elevator to the second floor.

senses.definition: In, to, or from a different place.
senses.example: The playground was full, so we went elsewhere.

senses.definition: A serious, sudden situation that needs quick action.
senses.example: Our class learned where to meet during an emergency.

senses.definition: A strong feeling such as joy, worry, or anger.
senses.example: Her drawing showed the emotion she felt after hearing the music.

senses.definition: A number of lands or peoples governed from one main center of power.
senses.example: The empire grew as it took control of nearby cities.

senses.definition: Having nothing or no one inside.
senses.example: My glass was empty after lunch.

senses.definition: To take out all or nearly all of what is inside something.
senses.example: Please empty the paper bin.

senses.definition: A mixture that holds tiny drops of one liquid spread through another liquid.
senses.example: Shaking the jar formed an emulsion of drops of oil in water.

senses.definition: The hard outer coat on the part of a tooth above the gums.
senses.example: Enamel protects a tooth when I chew.

senses.definition: To help someone feel able or willing to do something, often with support or kind words.
senses.example: Our cheers encouraged the last runner to keep going.

senses.definition: The last part of something, or the point past which it does not continue.
senses.example: There was a bench at the end of the path.

senses.definition: To come to a stop or bring something to a stop.
senses.example: The show will end at four o’clock.

senses.definition: A person or group that tries to harm or defeat another.
senses.example: In the story, the two enemies agreed to stop fighting.

senses.definition: Something that can be passed or stored and that makes changes possible, such as moving things, heating them, or making light.
senses.example: Sunlight brings energy to Earth.

senses.definition: The strength or liveliness you have for doing things.
senses.example: After a snack and a rest, I had more energy for the walk.

senses.definition: A machine that uses energy to make a vehicle or another machine move.
senses.example: The driver stopped the bus and turned off the engine.

senses.definition: A person who uses science and math to design, build, or test things.
senses.example: An engineer checked whether the bridge could hold the trucks.

senses.definition: To design, build, or plan something with care.
senses.example: The team engineered a folding ramp for the cart.

senses.definition: To have fun or get pleasure from doing or having something.
senses.example: I enjoy listening to stories on a rainy day.

senses.definition: Very large.
senses.example: An enormous tree shaded the schoolyard.

senses.definition: As much or as many as needed.
senses.example: I packed enough snacks for four hikers.

senses.definition: As much as is needed.
senses.example: We brought some paper, and that was enough.

senses.definition: To the degree needed for something to work or happen.
senses.example: The shelf is low enough for me to reach.

senses.definition: To go into a place, join an event, or put information into a system.
senses.example: We entered our names on the sign-up sheet.

senses.definition: All of something, with nothing left out.
senses.example: The entire family helped with the big puzzle.

senses.definition: A place to go in, or the act of coming in.
senses.example: The entrance to the building is on the left.

senses.definition: A flat paper holder with a flap, often used to mail a letter.
senses.example: I put the letter inside an envelope.

senses.definition: A feeling of wanting something that another person has.
senses.example: I felt a little envy when my brother got the seat by the window.

senses.definition: To wish you had something that belongs to someone else, such as a skill or a chance.
senses.example: I envy the way she plays piano with both hands.

senses.definition: A tiny biological helper that speeds up a change, such as breaking food into smaller pieces.
senses.example: An enzyme in saliva starts breaking down some starch from bread.

senses.definition: The same in amount, number, size, or value.
senses.example: We divided the melon into four equal pieces.

senses.definition: To be the same in amount or value as something else.
senses.example: Two nickels equal one dime.

senses.definition: An imaginary line all the way around Earth halfway between the North Pole and South Pole.
senses.example: The equator passes through parts of South America, Africa, and Asia.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when Earth’s poles are tilted neither toward nor away from the Sun.
senses.example: Around the equinox, day and night at many places are almost the same length.

senses.definition: Equal in value or meaning, even if shown in a different way.
senses.example: Two quarters and one half are equivalent amounts.

senses.definition: A tool for removing pencil marks, writing on a board, or similar marks.
senses.example: I kept an eraser next to my pencil.

senses.definition: The wearing away and carrying off of soil or pieces of rock by moving water, wind, or ice, or by gravity.
senses.example: Erosion slowly carried sand away from the bank.

senses.definition: A mistake or something that is not correct.
senses.example: I found one error in the list of bus times.

senses.definition: To get free or get away from a place or danger.
senses.example: The puppy escaped through the open gate.

senses.definition: An act of getting away, or something that gives you a break from worry or hard work.
senses.example: Reading a funny book was a welcome escape from my busy day.

senses.definition: The tube that carries swallowed food and drinks from the throat to the stomach.
senses.example: Muscles in your esophagus squeeze to move food toward your stomach.

senses.definition: More than usual, or more than other things or people in a group.
senses.example: I like puzzles, especially ones with picture clues.

senses.definition: A piece of writing that explains a subject or tells what the writer thinks about it.
senses.example: We wrote an essay about what makes a good friend.

senses.definition: To use clues to make a reasonable guess about a number, amount, or size.
senses.example: We estimated how many cups of water could fit in the bowl.

senses.definition: A reasonable guess about a number, amount, or size.
senses.example: My estimate was close to the number of tiles we actually used.

senses.definition: A partly sheltered area near the coast where fresh water from land often mixes with salt water from the sea.
senses.example: Small fish found shelter in the shallow estuary.

senses.definition: The change from liquid to gas that happens at a liquid’s surface.
senses.example: Evaporation helped the puddle disappear after the rain.

senses.definition: Flat, smooth, or equal.
senses.example: We tried to make the two rows of blocks even.

senses.definition: Able to be divided into two equal whole-number groups, with nothing left over.
senses.example: Eight is even because it can be divided into two groups of four.

senses.definition: Used to show that something is unexpected or to add a strong example.
senses.example: It was so quiet we could even hear the clock tick.

senses.definition: To make something level or equal.
senses.example: Adding one card to his stack will even the two piles.

senses.definition: A whole number that can be put into pairs with none left over.
senses.example: Eight is an even number because it makes four pairs.

senses.definition: The part of the day after the afternoon and before night.
senses.example: We took a short walk in the evening.

senses.definition: Something that happens, often something planned or important.
senses.example: The school concert is a big event in May.

senses.definition: The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape to the outside.
senses.example: Light that passes inside the event horizon cannot come back out.

senses.definition: At any time.
senses.example: Have you ever watched a robin build a nest?

senses.definition: Always or for a very long time.
senses.example: In the story, they lived happily ever after.

senses.definition: A plant that keeps some green leaves throughout the year.
senses.example: The spruce is an evergreen, so its branches looked green in January.

senses.definition: Facts, objects, or observations that help you check whether an idea is true.
senses.example: The muddy paw prints were evidence that a dog had crossed the porch.

senses.definition: Change in the traits that living things pass to their young over many generations.
senses.example: Fossils help scientists study the evolution of whales over millions of years.

senses.definition: Correct in every detail or a perfect match.
senses.example: We wrote down the exact time the bus left.

senses.definition: To look at or study something closely to learn about it.
senses.example: We examined the seed with a magnifying glass.

senses.definition: Something that shows what a larger group or idea is like.
senses.example: A robin is one example of a bird you might see in a park.

senses.definition: Very good.
senses.example: You did an excellent job putting the pictures in order.

senses.definition: Leaving someone or something out.
senses.example: Everyone except Nia had already eaten.

senses.definition: To give one thing and get another in return.
senses.example: We exchanged books after we both finished reading.

senses.definition: An act of trading things or sharing words or ideas.
senses.example: The two classes planned a letter exchange.

senses.definition: Feeling strong happiness or interest about something.
senses.example: I was excited to see my first basketball game.

senses.definition: To say something suddenly or strongly because of a feeling such as surprise or excitement.
senses.example: I exclaimed that I could see the finish line.

senses.definition: A word or remark said suddenly or with strong feeling.
senses.example: His first exclamation was “We did it!”

senses.definition: A reason given to explain why something went wrong or was not done.
senses.example: The broken clock was his excuse for being late.

senses.definition: To forgive or let someone leave or skip a duty.
senses.example: Our coach excused Sam from practice so he could rest.

senses.definition: Activity that helps keep the body strong and healthy.
senses.example: Walking uphill gives us exercise.

senses.definition: A set task that helps you practice a skill.
senses.example: The first math exercise uses clocks.

senses.definition: To move your body to help keep it strong or healthy.
senses.example: We exercise by swimming twice a week.

senses.definition: An object or group of things set out for people to see and learn about.
senses.example: We looked at an exhibit about old cameras.

senses.definition: To show something where people can see it, or to show a quality by what you do.
senses.example: Our class will exhibit the artwork in the hall.

senses.definition: A way to go out of a place.
senses.example: The sign shows where the nearest exit is.

senses.definition: To go out or leave a place, program, or activity.
senses.example: We exited the theater after the credits.

senses.definition: A planet outside our solar system.
senses.example: Astronomers detected an exoplanet by watching its star become a little dimmer.

senses.definition: A place between parts that leaves room for them to move as they get bigger or smaller.
senses.example: An expansion joint let the road deck shift a little in warm weather.

senses.definition: To think that something will probably happen or someone will do something.
senses.example: I expect to see a line at the ice cream shop.

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.
senses.example: A new piano can be expensive.

senses.definition: Something that happens to you or that you do.
senses.example: Seeing a rainbow from an airplane was a new experience.

senses.definition: Knowledge or skill gained from doing something.
senses.example: She has plenty of experience repairing bikes.

senses.definition: To live through, feel, or take part in something.
senses.example: The visitors experienced a wide range of weather on their trip.

senses.definition: A planned test to find out what happens under certain conditions.
senses.example: In our experiment, we measured how quickly ice melted in sun and shade.

senses.definition: To try different things or do a test to find out what happens.
senses.example: We experimented with several ways to fold the paper.

senses.definition: A person who knows a great deal about a subject or is very skilled at something.
senses.example: An expert on bees visited our class.

senses.definition: Done with great skill or knowledge.
senses.example: I need expert help to fix this old clock.

senses.definition: To make an idea or event easier to understand with reasons, details, or examples.
senses.example: Can you explain why you put those shapes in the same group?

senses.definition: To travel through a place or study a subject to find out more.
senses.example: We took our map so we could explore a new part of the park.

senses.definition: To show or tell a thought, feeling, or idea.
senses.example: I find it easiest to express my ideas by drawing first.

senses.definition: Fast, especially by making fewer stops or taking less time.
senses.example: We took an express bus straight to the station.

senses.definition: A look on someone’s face that shows a feeling.
senses.example: The puzzled expression on my friend’s face made me ask what was wrong.

senses.definition: A word or group of words used to say something in a certain way.
senses.example: “Good luck” is an expression people use before a contest.

senses.definition: In math, a group of numbers, signs, or letters that shows a value.
senses.example: “Five plus two” is an expression with a value of seven.

senses.definition: To stretch, reach, or make something last longer or go farther.
senses.example: We extended the table so two more people could sit down.

senses.definition: More than the amount usually needed or expected.
senses.example: Bring an extra pair of socks.

senses.definition: Something added beyond the usual or needed amount.
senses.example: I packed an extra in case someone forgot a pencil.

senses.definition: The body part you use to see.
senses.example: The cat opened one eye when I stepped into the room.

senses.definition: The hole in a needle that thread passes through.
senses.example: The thread slipped through the eye of the needle.

senses.definition: To look at someone or something carefully or with interest.
senses.example: The dog eyed my sandwich.

senses.definition: The height of someone’s eyes when they are looking straight ahead.
senses.example: The museum put the labels near eye level for younger visitors.

senses.definition: The short row of hair above each eye.
senses.example: My aunt lifted one eyebrow when she saw the muddy shoes.
